verdicts.flaw_description: Two of the four cases have the outcome measured before the bearing was fitted: case One was 'fitted 4 May' but its extra 340 hours are counted 'by 27 March', and case Three was 'fitted 2 August' but counted 'by 21 July'. The two well-ordered cases (9 January to 24 February, 6 October to 25 November) run about six weeks, so the reversed pairs cannot be read as spanning into the following year.

Rainfall 'was the highest on record, roughly double the year before' in each plot's season, and 'every plot stood in the open, watered by rain alone', so the record rain reaches all four plants and equally explains the 8-13 cm gain over the previous summer. The confound is not merely present but demonstrably delivered to every unit.

Cohorts One and Three record the outcome before the email went out: emailed '24 March' but week-two retention read 'by 9 March', and emailed '25 October' but read 'by 10 October'. The other two cohorts run about 24 days forward (3 July to 27 July, 2 December to 26 December), and week-two retention needs at least 14 days after signup, so these are reversed, not next-year, intervals.

The measured population is narrower than the claim: 'Timings cover the runs that stayed on the issued route', while 'about a sixth of each depot's runs left the issued route' and are therefore excluded. The runs most likely to abandon a new route are the ones where it went badly, so the 5-9 minute saving is computed on a filtered subset rather than on the routing change's actual effect.
